knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.2.5
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly writes linear predictors for a simple slope, a two-level factor with baseline coding, and a quadratic term in x?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Linear-predictor fluency covers continuous slopes, baseline factor coding, and polynomial terms inside eta.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping factor or polynomial forms, or moving structure into the link by habit.

choices.label: Simple slope: eta = beta0 + beta1 x. Two-level factor with baseline coding: eta = beta0 + beta_A I_A (versus baseline). Quadratic: eta = beta0 + beta1 x + beta2 x^2.
All three cases use only eta = beta0, because factors and polynomials are handled entirely by the link function.
A two-level factor must enter as a multiplicative link term rather than an indicator in eta, and a quadratic term is written without coefficients.
Quadratic terms are forbidden in linear predictors, and factor coding always absorbs the intercept so beta0 disappears.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.2.5
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly refuses treating the link function as the linear predictor and restates both objects?
knowledge_checks.body: Refuse conflation; restate eta and the link.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Eta is X beta; the link maps mean to eta. Conflating them breaks GLM structure.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Refuse conflation. Eta = X beta; link g maps mu to eta.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting that the link function is the linear predictor.

choices.label: Refuse: the link is not the linear predictor. Eta = X beta is the linear predictor; the link g maps the mean mu to eta.
Accept: link and linear predictor are two names for the same eta object.
Refuse the word link, but treat g(mu) as identical to X beta with no mapping role for the mean.
The linear predictor maps mu to a restricted range, while the link is only the coefficient vector beta.
